clue.text: Not a soul sister by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the word for sister is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person seems not to be a soul sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' says the word for sister, NUN, is heard and spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying not a single person was there is the same as saying nobody at all was.

clue.text: Uncared-for nationalist gets voted in and is blocked by government

indicators.note: something blocked has an obstruction sitting inside it, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a candidate who is voted in has been elected

explanation.surface: A nationalist politician wins office but finds the government obstructing them, leaving their cause ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is blocked by' puts G inside ELECTED, giving EGLECTED after the opening N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left without attention or upkeep has been ignored and let go.

clue.text: Take care of polluted universe I've left behind

indicators.note: polluted means fouled or corrupted, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written; these letters come out of the fodder

explanation.surface: An eco-warrior vows to tend a dirtied universe that they have abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I, V and E (the letters of 'I've', which is 'left behind') from UNIVERSE and rearrange the remaining UNRSE, as 'polluted' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone or something carefully, as a carer does a patient, is a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Papers keeping quiet over electronic listening device

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the papers word wraps the other letters

parts.note: ID means identity papers
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Documents are retained for a while over some quiet listening gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts P and O inside ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's portable music player is a brand-name gadget for hearing songs through earphones.

clue.text: Share-pushers place sign outside that's offensive

parts.note: PL is the usual abbreviation for place in addresses

indicators.note: outside means the sign word sits around the next piece, wrapping it

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come
ugh is the exclamation someone makes at something disgusting

explanation.surface: A stock-market tipster puts up a notice outside some objectionable venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share-pushers' looks like stockbrokers, but a ploughshare is the blade of a plough, pushed by farm workers; 'outside' wraps the sign round the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm labourers drive a plough, whose cutting blade is called a share.

clue.text: Party happens in Dutch company

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the pair of abbreviations

parts.note: is can mean takes place, as in the meeting is on Monday

explanation.surface: A party takes place at a firm in the Netherlands; Dutch is also this setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happens' stands for 'is', as in 'the party is tonight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance night with recorded pop music and flashing lights is a kind of social gathering.

clue.text: Make three a different number

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the letters is asked for, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn three into some other figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure, but it means something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, something that deadens feeling in a patient.

clue.text: Create time and energy for compiling and suchlike

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: a crossword compiler assembles and arranges, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A compiler is advised to set aside time and energy for creating puzzles and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiling' rearranges CREATE with T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase closes a list to mean 'and other things of the same kind'.

clue.text: Firm has daily financial troubles

parts.note: firm means solid or unyielding
The Times is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A business has money problems every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company and 'daily' like an adverb; THE TIMES is a London daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of poverty and hardship, as in Dickens's novel title, is a spell of money worries.

clue.text: Bible class covers short song of praise seen in 16 and 25D?

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so the class letters go either side of the song

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject for Bible lessons

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: a hymn is a song praising God

explanation.surface: A Bible class includes a brief hymn that turns up in two other puzzle entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts HYMN to HYM, which RE 'covers'. The answers at 16 and 25 down, SMOKER and POKER, end in the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words sharing their ending sound, as these two entries do, form this poetic device.

clue.text: Prone to gas?

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chatter, so someone given to it talks too much, not someone suffering wind

explanation.surface: A question about someone liable to flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wind; here gas is chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chatters on at length about trivial things is excessively talkative.

clue.text: One upper-class twit

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage in British English
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A single aristocratic fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item counted as a whole is one of something.

clue.text: Bear arriving in Cyprus

indicators.note: in places the arrival letters inside the country code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arriving

explanation.surface: A bear turns up on Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to hold it up and transport it.

clue.text: Balancing is essential to drinking nine vermouths on the bounce

indicators.note: a ball on the bounce comes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
something essential to a phrase lies within it, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Keeping one's balance matters when downing nine vermouths in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the bounce' looks like 'in succession' but turns back the letters GNINEVE that 'is essential to' finds in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Making things level or equal, as in levelling a score, is a sense of the verb form.

clue.text: Old alcoholic finally sober in support group

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word before it
in puts the sober letters within the support

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
TT means teetotal, so sober

explanation.surface: A former drinker, now sober, attends a support group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support group' reads as one phrase, but 'support' is TEE, which TT goes 'in'. The answer is a variant spelling of octet.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight musicians or singers is an ensemble of that size.

clue.text: Instant credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'wait a second'
informal British for buying on account, as in 'on the slate'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal British: a very short moment, and goods bought now and paid for later.

clue.text: Poser with Spanish and German liquor

parts.note: con is Spanish for with
und is German for and
rum is a spirit, a liquor

explanation.surface: Someone striking a pose with a Spanish companion and a German spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' looks like a model; it means a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or riddle is something that poses a problem.

clue.text: Puffer fish curer?

definitions.meaning: someone who puffs on cigarettes or a pipe
a kiln or person preserving fish over wood smoke

explanation.definitionFit: One habitually inhales tobacco; the other preserves kippers and salmon by exposing them to fumes.

clue.text: Freezing instructions — is best before …?

definitions.meaning: an order to stop moving, as in 'freeze!'
split differently the phrase reads '...', like a food label's best-before date

explanation.walkthrough: 'Freezing instructions' look like freezer labels; the second sense splits as KEEPS TILL, which a best-before date says of food.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense orders someone not to move; the other, split after its fifth letter, tells how long food lasts.

clue.text: Entertained by Tom and Jerry, maybe

definitions.text: Entertained by Tom and Jerry, maybe

indicators.note: entertained by means held as a guest inside, so the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps, being amused by the cartoon cat and mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'Tom and'; Tom and Jerry are also both men's names, which is what 'maybe' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom and Jerry are first names for a male person, examples of the answer.

clue.text: No way to kill yen for travelling

indicators.note: travelling letters move about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An assertion that there is no way of satisfying a longing for travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges TO KILL YEN; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic informal refusals, ways of saying something will never happen.

clue.text: Diagram providing route for a pub-crawl?

definitions.meaning: a graph showing values as rectangles
a map of drinking places to visit in turn

explanation.definitionFit: A graph using rectangles to compare quantities; read literally, a chart of bars for a night out.

clue.text: Pull on ends of cord to tighten

indicators.note: ends of picks the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Tug on a drawstring to tighten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull on' suggests tugging; it means put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a garment is to dress in it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: A pea brought about no sleeping problem

indicators.note: brought about means placed all round, so the pea's letters surround the next word

explanation.surface: A pea under the mattress caused no trouble sleeping, unlike for the fairy-tale princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', but here it means placed around the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder in which breathing stops during the night disturbs a person's rest.

clue.text: Sopranos in training — that might attract attention

indicators.note: in places these letters within the training abbreviation

parts.note: PT means physical training
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Trainee sopranos are told something that should draw notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing what the answer does, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered hiss used to get someone's notice without shouting.

clue.text: Female friend posed by warm fire, oddly withdrawn

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters taken away, only the even-placed letters remain

explanation.surface: A girlfriend poses beside a cosy fire, then leaves strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly withdrawn' removes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'warm fire'; 'posed by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a girlfriend or woman friend, used in English too.

clue.text: Old man takes loo over with each elixir

parts.note: pa is informal for father, one's old man

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the loo word is read backwards

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Father seizes the toilet along with a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns CAN into NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposed remedy for every ailment, like an alchemist's potion, is a cure-all.

clue.text: I agree to enter a card game

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the agreement goes within the other piece

parts.note: a can mean per, as in five pounds a head
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: Someone consents to join a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' means 'each', as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting game of hands and bluffing, played with a standard pack.

clue.text: Warning signal a doctor hears regularly

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, so a doctor

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A GP listens to a warning signal at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'hears'.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange traffic light warns drivers that red is coming.

clue.text: Sport masters back top-notch fighter

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so these two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union
MAs are holders of Master of Arts degrees
A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: Masters of a sport support a first-class combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUMAS into SAMUR; 'back' also looks like support.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese warrior of the feudal military class.

clue.text: Dutch very well after port wine

indicators.note: after puts the Dutch word behind the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is Dutch for yes, very well

explanation.surface: A Dutchman approves of drinking wine after port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine; it is RIO the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from a region of northern Spain.

clue.text: According to rumour, my old lady's a dish

indicators.note: rumour is what people say, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like 'my!', and ma is mum, one's old lady

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that someone's mother is very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dish' looks like 'attractive'; COR plus MA, said aloud, gives a mild curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild creamy Indian curry is something served on a plate.

clue.text: Woman tying the knot soon may become bored, I bet

indicators.note: may become means turning into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fiancée may soon grow bored with marriage, the cynic bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may become' rearranges BORED I BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged and about to marry is due to be wed.

clue.text: Brief sleep then sex

parts.note: REM is the rapid-eye-movement phase of sleep
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A short nap and then intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like 'short', but it is a noun, a task assigned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's set area of responsibility is their remit, like a lawyer's instructions.

clue.text: Depend on vacated lavatory

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone needs an empty toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depend on' looks like the definition; 'on' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on or trust something is to be dependent on it.

clue.text: May essentially divides Britain with pet project

indicators.note: divides means splits apart, so the core letter goes between the others

parts.note: by can mean with, as in by means of

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of a word, its middle letter

explanation.surface: Prime Minister May splits Britain over her favourite scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divides' puts A, the middle of 'May', between B and BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's darling scheme is their own creation, something they nurture.
